request.text: Collab orchestration and patrol use one project-generic contract. Master and ordinary peer are both autonomous long-horizon goal orchestrators at different goal levels; peer is not a bounded execution worker. Each can register, read, update, rearm and cancel its own goal. A project master can configure a project peer's long-horizon subscription. Master dispatch task sheets must include the long-horizon task content and a declared cadence, and dispatch automatically starts the selected peer's subscription. Task dispatch and its subscription transition share one durable commit, with explicit errors on failure. The current typed CEO can modify anyone's long-horizon subscription across projects. The target peer remains the stable-name owner and current delivery recipient. New periodic long-horizon subscriptions default to100 total cycles, with explicit counts supported. Generic notification defaults are unchanged. Existing one-shot records are not automatically converted. Repeat reconciliation and binding recovery preserve current progress without duplicate timers. Fired task reminders contain the actual task instructions. Stable name owns work; agent sessionID is its current execution carrier, independent of tmux and worktree placement. Read-only goal status does not rewrite records. Authorized lifecycle changes affect only the selected target and goal. Ordinary tasks or notes do not prove a goal subscription exists; dispatch must return the actual target subscription receipt. Route suitable long-horizon subgoals to consenting authorized peers; route bounded execution and observation directly to independent codex exec --profile gcm subworkers regardless of peer availability, using only the documented fallback when unavailable. Keep Plan/Review roles and host primitives separate; do not use built-in spawn/fork/session Agent slots or legacy managed subagents as production concurrency. Both orchestrators plan, dispatch, manage resources, verify evidence, unblock, integrate and deliver their own goal. On each assignment evaluate goal/dependencies/blockers/priority/resources and update finite owned patrols without duplicate timers. Patrol checks open P0/P1 work, actual subtask progress, owned worktree/runtime cleanup, canonical issue intake and relevant events; preserve protected dirty, active, shared or unknown resources. Peer requests master help for blockers without transferring goal ownership. Rearm a consumed one-shot wake only while actionable scheduling remains; ACK/read/summary are not completion. On goal completion or no new task and no actionable work, actively close owned goal scheduling and patrols while keeping direct-message reception. Audit all active AppSDK project prompts, runtime generators, templates, source and installed Skills for conflicting roles, logic gaps and duplicated rule owners; remove incorrect instructions, retain one authoritative owner and distinguish generated projections from independent sources. Preserve legitimate current-master project arbitration, reset, master-idle and cross-project boundaries; global daemon lifecycle remains user-managed and is not an identity or project reset prerequisite. Keep this contract project-generic; business-specific checks belong to their project Skill.

request.text: Collab orchestration and patrol use one project-generic contract. Master and ordinary peer are both autonomous long-horizon goal orchestrators at different goal levels; peer is not a bounded execution worker. Each can register, read, update, rearm and cancel its own goal. A project master can configure a project peer's long-horizon subscription. Master dispatch task sheets must include the long-horizon task content and a declared cadence, and dispatch automatically starts the selected peer's subscription. Task dispatch and its subscription transition share one durable commit, with explicit errors on failure. The current typed CEO can modify anyone's long-horizon subscription across projects. The target peer remains the stable-name owner and current delivery recipient. New periodic long-horizon subscriptions default to100 total cycles, with explicit counts supported. Generic notification defaults are unchanged. Existing one-shot records are not automatically converted. Repeat reconciliation and binding recovery preserve current progress without duplicate timers. Fired task reminders contain the actual task instructions. Stable name owns work; agent sessionID is its current execution carrier, independent of tmux and worktree placement. Read-only goal status does not rewrite records. Authorized lifecycle changes affect only the selected target and goal. Ordinary tasks or notes do not prove a goal subscription exists; dispatch must return the actual target subscription receipt. Route suitable long-horizon subgoals to consenting authorized peers; route bounded execution and observation directly to independent codex exec --profile gcm subworkers regardless of peer availability, using only the documented fallback when unavailable. Keep Plan/Review roles and host primitives separate; do not use built-in spawn/fork/session Agent slots or legacy managed subagents as production concurrency. Both orchestrators plan, dispatch, manage resources, verify evidence, unblock, integrate and deliver their own goal. On each assignment evaluate goal/dependencies/blockers/priority/resources and update finite owned patrols without duplicate timers. Patrol checks open P0/P1 work, actual subtask progress, owned worktree/runtime cleanup, canonical issue intake and relevant events; preserve protected dirty, active, shared or unknown resources. Peer requests master help for blockers without transferring goal ownership. Rearm a consumed one-shot wake only while actionable scheduling remains; ACK/read/summary are not completion. On goal completion or no new task and no actionable work, actively close owned goal scheduling and patrols while keeping direct-message reception. Audit all active AppSDK project prompts, runtime generators, templates, source and installed Skills for conflicting roles, logic gaps and duplicated rule owners; remove incorrect instructions, retain one authoritative owner and distinguish generated projections from independent sources. Preserve legitimate current-master project arbitration, reset, master-idle and cross-project boundaries; global daemon lifecycle remains user-managed and is not an identity or project reset prerequisite. Keep this contract project-generic; business-specific checks belong to their project Skill. A repeat count above 100 is accepted without error; 100 is only the default.
